# Tetorica Playground (hello_ymfm_wasm)

> Browser-based JavaScript playground, documentation, and WebAssembly tools for OPN FM, Mega CD, Game Boy, NES + FDS, SNES, X68000, PC Engine, Game Gear and Master System sound chips.

Use the common Playground type definitions together with the type definition for the selected sound chip. The canonical examples are code that runs in the Playground.

## Documentation

- [VGM Analyzer sound chip support](./vgm_analyzer/support.html): Browser playback, analysis, export coverage and limitations by chip

- [For AI](./for-ai.html): AI-oriented entry point, execution contract, type definitions, and representative examples
- [Documentation](./index.html): Human-oriented project documentation and demos
- [Playground](./playground/): Interactive JavaScript Playground

## Type definitions

- [Common Playground API](./playground/tetorica-playground-globals.d.ts): Globals, live coding, samples, noise, effects, files, FM, and PSG APIs
- [YM2612 selection](./playground/tetorica-playground-ym2612.d.ts): Mega Drive / Genesis configuration
- [Mega CD selection](./playground/tetorica-playground-mega-cd.d.ts): YM2612 FM, Sega PSG and the primary RF5C164, without 32X PWM. Also used by 32X and 32X Nuked modes for shared PCM ownership. Await useSoundChip('rf5c164') for the built-in eight-voice PCM; createSoundChip adds a separate disposable device.
- [YM2608 selection](./playground/tetorica-playground-ym2608.d.ts): PC-98 configuration
- [YM2203 selection](./playground/tetorica-playground-ym2203.d.ts): Three-channel PC-98 configuration
- [YM2610 selection](./playground/tetorica-playground-ym2610.d.ts): Neo Geo configuration
- [Game Boy mode](./playground/tetorica-playground-gameboy.d.ts): Built-in gameboy.pulse, gameboy.wave and gameboy.noise; no global play/fm/OPN shortcuts. Use beat/sleep/liveLoop for timing.
- [NES + FDS mode](./playground/tetorica-playground-nes.d.ts): Primary nes.pulse/triangle/noise/dmc/fds. FDS is enabled in this mode; use {fds:true} for independent createSoundChip('nes').
- [SNES mode](./playground/tetorica-playground-snes.d.ts): Primary snes CPU-free S-DSP with eight BRR voices. Await loadBRR, assign with setPreset, then noteOn. Native PCM is 32,000 Hz; no setClock. SPC file playback uses useSoundChip('spc').
- [X68000 mode](./playground/tetorica-playground-x68000.d.ts): Primary opm (YM2151, 4 MHz) and adpcm (OKIM6258, 8 MHz). Await adpcm.loadSample(PCM/WAV) or loadMemory(OKI ADPCM4, low nibble first), then play({repeat?}) / stop(). This is not the OPN ADPCM-B API.
- [PC Engine mode](./playground/tetorica-playground-huc6280.d.ts): Primary pce HuC6280 with six 32-sample five-bit wavetable voices, noise on channels 4/5, DDA and LFO. Additional chip name is huc6280.
- [Game Gear mode](./playground/tetorica-playground-game-gear.d.ts): Primary psg Sega PSG with three tones and noise. psg.setStereo(mask) routes bits 0..3 to the right and bits 4..7 to the left; 0xff enables both sides. Use PSG1..3 for tone channels.
- [Master System mode](./playground/tetorica-playground-master-system.d.ts): Primary psg Sega PSG with three tones and noise, mixed in mono. No setStereo on the primary instrument. This mode uses the base PSG and does not include the optional YM2413 FM expansion.

Native modes expose the same instrument namespaces on pg and livePrepare. Game Boy, NES, SNES, X68000, PC Engine, Game Gear and Master System have no global fm/play/write, OPN pitch helpers, FM channel/operator constants or MIDI-to-FM shortcuts. Use explicit instrument methods and beat/sleep/liveLoop. useSoundChip of a mode's primary instrument borrows it without dispose; createSoundChip creates an additional disposable instrument. In Game Gear and Master System modes, useSoundChip('segapsg') returns the primary psg; createSoundChip('segapsg') creates an independent PSG with stereo routing. OPN chips remain available explicitly from every mode. Non-Genesis modes each bundle 2–3 native examples and their own defaults/<mode>/index.js.

inputAudio({title?,asset?,edit?}) and pg.inputAudio open the shared Sample Editor in Main and Worker execution. It supports local files, microphone recording (up to 60 seconds, only after clicking Record), waveform selection/zoom, gain/normalize, fades, loop bounds, root MIDI note/tuning, pitch suggestions, Undo/Redo and drawn cycles. Cancel returns null. Success returns {name,source:'file'|'microphone',sampleRate,channels:Float32Array[],rootMidi,tuneCents,loopEnabled,loopStartFrame,loopEndFrame,target,assetPath}; Game Boy conversion also returns waveform (32 four-bit values). The default /samples/sampler.sample.json stores neutral settings separately from its original Float32 WAV in the Cassette. edit:false loads a saved asset without opening the dialog; a missing asset opens the editor. Menu → Sample Editor or opening a .sample.json in FILES re-edits the source.

keyboard.bind(name,{noteOn(event),noteOff(event),allNotesOff()}) connects the existing Guitar/PC Keyboard to any instrument; pg.keyboard is the same API. Events contain a unique press id, integer midi 0..127 and velocity 0..127, so repeated pitches have independent ownership. A successful Run replaces the binding; Stop/blur/layout changes release held notes. Keyboard callbacks use immediate input timing rather than musical lookahead. await createSampleInstrument(audio,{target?,volume?}) prepares an RF5C164 eight-voice sampler, Game Boy 32-point wave or PC98/Neo Geo ADPCM-B single voice; then keyboard.bind('sampler',instrument). Preparation/encoding happens before input callbacks. RF samples share 64 KiB RAM, allow at most 65,504 frames including the end-guard budget, and change duration with pitch. ADPCM-B loops must cover the full selected sample. Tune metadata is applied as 2**(((midi-rootMidi)*100-tuneCents)/1200). Custom asynchronous handlers should cancel delayed work on allNotesOff and retain initialized chip clients.

## Examples

- [Canonical example source](./playground/playground_examples.js): Built-in examples used by the Playground
Open these source files from Playground FILES → examples to run them.

- [Live Loop](./playground/examples/basic/live-loop.js): Tempo, notes, and named loops
- [Ambient Choir Sample](./playground/examples/basic/ambient-choir-sample.js): Sample loading, effects, and live state
- [FM API Beep](./playground/examples/basic/fm/fm-api-beep.js): Direct YM2612 setup
- [PSG Scale](./playground/examples/basic/psg/psg-scale.js): SN76489-compatible tone API
- [Mega CD starter](./playground/defaults/mega-cd/index.js): FM and a short PCM bass with a baked attack/release in the built-in RF5C164
- [Mega CD sampler](./playground/examples/mega-cd/megacd-sampler.js): Choose a local sound or record the microphone, then play it with the keyboard using up to eight PCM voices
- [Parallel FX](./playground/examples/basic/fx/parallel-fx.js): Branched effect routing
- [Game Boy mode pulse](./playground/examples/gameboy/gameboy-mode-pulse.js): Primary APU with explicit pulse noteOn/keyOff and a named melody loop
- [NES + FDS starter](./playground/defaults/nes/index.js): Primary APU melody; selected examples add FDS and rhythm/DMC
- [SNES starter](./playground/defaults/snes/index.js): Authored BRR sample and eight-voice S-DSP programming
- [X68000 starter](./playground/defaults/x68000/index.js): YM2151 OPM programming; selected ADPCM example encodes PCM for OKIM6258
- [PC Engine starter](./playground/defaults/pc-engine/index.js): HuC6280 waveform and explicit channel noteOn/keyOff
- [Game Gear starter](./playground/defaults/game-gear/index.js): Three-tone Sega PSG melody, noise rhythm, and stereo routing
- [Game Gear stereo](./playground/examples/game-gear/gg-mode-stereo.js): Route physical tone channels to the left or right speaker
- [Master System starter](./playground/defaults/master-system/index.js): Sega PSG melody and noise rhythm in mono
- [DX7 Init Sine](./playground/examples/dx7/dx7-init-sine.js): useSoundChip('dx7'), 16-voice MIDI-note playback and DX7 SysEx banks. Read SysEx with file(path, {type:'arrayBuffer'}); await loadSysex before noteOn. MSFA runs internally at 44,100 Hz and has no setClock API.
